caption: The drawing depicts a close-up view of a carved wooden figure of a person's head and shoulders. The figure is adorned with a large, brimmed hat that features a prominent, textured plume or feather, both rendered in shades of muted gray, beige, and hints of brown, with visible signs of paint peeling and surface crackling. The face is shown in profile, with subtle detail given to the features, and is colored in pale, weathered tones suggesting aged or worn paint. The hair is carved with parallel grooves and painted in a light tone matching the overall palette. Around the figure’s neck is a ruffled collar, also depicted with cracked and flaking paint. The background is plain, and the lower left portion of the drawing includes diagonal wooden planks, indicating the figure is attached to a wooden surface or structure. The composition positions the head and hat diagonally across the page, with the upper portion of the hat nearly touching the top edge of the image.
title: Figurehead
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
